name: VNDegen
subtitle: Visual novels and RPG Maker games, native on iPhone and iPad.
description: VNDegen runs visual novel and RPG Maker games natively. Copy a game's folder into the Games folder in the Files app, or import a zip, RAR, or 7z archive, and VNDegen detects its engine and shows it in a game hub with artwork from Steam, SteamGridDB, IGDB, and VNDB. Supports touch, controllers, and keyboard, hidden games behind Face ID or a passcode, and Ludusavi save backups.

versions.localizedDescription:
Adds Wolf RPG Editor games on Mac, iPhone and iPad, three library layouts, a choice of SoundFont for MIDI music, and screenshots on game pages.

## Downloads

- `VNDegen-0.11.0-macOS.zip` for Mac (macOS 15 or later). It is ad-hoc signed: right-click VNDegen and choose Open the first time, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VNDegen.app`.
- `VNDegen-0.11.0.ipa` for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). Update it from the AltStore or SideStore source (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChronoStriker1/vndegen/main/altstore/source.json`), or sideload it with Sideloadly.

## New: Wolf RPG Editor

- Wolf RPG Editor 2 and 3 games run on VNDegen's own Wolf RPG Editor runtime, written in C++ for VNDegen and MIT licensed. No open-source runtime existed, so this one was written from the games' files, permissively licensed format notes and the original engine's behaviour. `docs/wolfrpg-cleanroom.md` lists its sources.
- VNDegen finds a game by `Data.wolf`, `Data/BasicData` or `Data/BasicData.wolf` beside `Game.exe`, up to two folders down. It reads loose files, Wolf RPG Editor 2's `.wolf` archives and its encrypted basic data.
- The runtime runs the games' event scripts, including the standard systems' menus, shops and battles. It draws each frame on the CPU and shows it through Metal, and plays Ogg, MP3, WAV and MIDI music.
- Saves are the PC engine's own `Save/SaveDataNN.sav` files beside `Game.exe`. Saves made on the PC load in VNDegen, and the other way round, so Ludusavi backups work for these games.
- Wolf RPG Editor games start with the gamepad layout: A confirms, B and Menu cancel and open the menu, and Dash is the sub key. The touch gamepad and the keyboard work too.
- Files are found whatever case the game names them in.

## New: MIDI music

- Wolf RPG Editor games play their MIDI music through a General MIDI SoundFont that VNDegen includes, FluidR3 Mono (MIT).
- Settings > MIDI music lets you choose your own `.sf2` or `.sf3` SoundFont instead. VNDegen keeps a copy of it, and Use the built-in SoundFont goes back. If your SoundFont can't be read, the built-in one plays. RPG Maker XP, VX and VX Ace games play MIDI with a synthesizer of their own and aren't affected.

## Library views

- The view button in the top bar, between Add game and All games, switches the library between three layouts. Header list stacks each game's wide header art, in one column on an iPhone in portrait and more on wider screens. Capsule rows shows shelves of large capsules. Featured is the hero art and shelves from before.
- iPhone starts on Header list, iPad on Capsule rows, and Mac on Featured. Each device remembers its choice.

## Game pages

- A game's About section shows a row of screenshots from Steam, or from IGDB when Steam has none. Its description and genres also come from Steam first, then IGDB. Games you matched before this update pick these up the first time you open their page.
- The artwork picker no longer shows the same picture twice when IGDB, VNDB or SteamGridDB hosts a copy of Steam's image. IGDB's thumbnails in the picker are sharper, and its hero images are no longer cropped.
- On iPhone in portrait, the art at the top of the home screen and of game pages is shorter, so the shelves and the game's title come into view sooner.

## Known limits: Wolf RPG Editor

- Wolf RPG Editor 3.5's compressed data, DxLib archive versions 7 and 8, and Wolf RPG Editor Pro's encrypted data aren't read yet.
- Mouse input and CSV import aren't supported, so games that need the mouse can't be played.
- Typing text on the keyboard isn't supported. Games that offer a default, such as a name, go on with it.
- A load restores the map, characters and variables, but not pictures, the screen tint or the music that was playing. The map's own music starts, as on the PC.
- Tested with 3 test games, which reach their title, play, save and load on the Mac and the iPad simulator, pass the case check, and hold 60 fps in battle. One also plays on the iPhone simulator. 13 more library games load and play in the Linux test build. `docs/wolfrpg.md` has the details.

Adds Artemis engine games on Mac, iPhone and iPad, and runs Godot games that use Steam or encrypted packs.

## Downloads

- `VNDegen-0.10.0-macOS.zip` for Mac (macOS 15 or later). It is ad-hoc signed: right-click VNDegen and choose Open the first time, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VNDegen.app`.
- `VNDegen-0.10.0.ipa` for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). Update it from the AltStore or SideStore source (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChronoStriker1/vndegen/main/altstore/source.json`), or sideload it with Sideloadly.

## New: Artemis

- Artemis games run inside VNDegen's window on art3m1s-core, an open-source Rust reimplementation of the Artemis runtime, built into the app. It draws through Metal and runs the games' Lua on Lua 5.1 with no JIT. The core is under MPL-2.0, and its source and every change VNDegen made to it are in `Engines/Artemis/`.
- VNDegen finds a game by its `.pfs` archive (`pf2`, `pf6` or `pf8`) and the patch volumes beside it, or by the `system.ini` of an unpacked game, up to two folders down.
- Saves are the PC engine's own files, in both versions it writes (1000 and 1002). A save made in VNDegen loads in the PC version at the same page, and the other way round, read history included. Saves go under the folder name the PC version uses, in AppData or beside the game, so Ludusavi backups from Windows restore there, including backups whose folder name a non-Japanese Windows garbled.
- Pages break where the PC version breaks them, and games that ship bitmap `.rft` fonts draw their English text from those fonts.
- Artemis games start with the "Keyboard and mouse" layout. Confirm reads on, Cancel presses Escape, Menu right clicks, Dash skips, and the page buttons open the message history. A game's own name-entry dialog answers to a controller.
- Files are found whatever case the game names them in.

## New: Godot

- Godot games that call Steam through GodotSteam run. VNDegen's Godot answers in Steam's place as Steam does offline, with the player signed in and owning the game. Achievements and stats last until the game quits.
- Godot 4 games that ship the Epic Online Services extension for their Epic build run. The extension's calls do nothing.
- Godot 4 games with an encrypted pack run. VNDegen finds the key in the game's `.exe`.
- `res://` paths the pack doesn't hold lead to the game's folder, as on Windows, so games that save through `res://` save.

## Known limits: Artemis

- Movies don't play, and each counts as finished at once.
- Screen effects written as HLSL shaders, such as sepia and negative, don't show.
- Steam functions in Steam builds do nothing.
- In games with bitmap `.rft` fonts, only ASCII comes from those fonts. Japanese text and symbols use MS Gothic, so a line with them can wrap differently than on the PC.
- A game's own native dialog, such as a name entry, shows as a system alert.
- In one test game, the screen stays black after a quick load until the next click, which shows the saved page.
- Tested with the 8 Artemis games in the library. All reach their title, play, save and load on the Mac and the iPad simulator, including from a library with every file name's case changed, and one also on the iPhone simulator. `docs/artemis.md` has the details.

## Known limits: Godot

- One Godot 3 game that uses Steam draws its backgrounds and play area black on the iPad simulator. It plays on the Mac.
- Leaderboard requests fail, and a game that calls a Steam function VNDegen's stand-in lacks stops that script and names the function in its log.
- An Epic Games Store build that signs in through Epic doesn't run.

Adds Godot games on Mac, iPhone and iPad.

## Downloads

- `VNDegen-0.9.0-macOS.zip` for Mac (macOS 15 or later). It is ad-hoc signed: right-click VNDegen and choose Open the first time, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VNDegen.app`.
- `VNDegen-0.9.0.ipa` for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). Update it from the AltStore or SideStore source (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChronoStriker1/vndegen/main/altstore/source.json`), or sideload it with Sideloadly.

## New

- Godot games run inside VNDegen's window. Godot 4 games run on Godot 4.7, and Godot 3 games on Godot 3.6, which covers games exported with Godot 4.2 to 4.5 and Godot 3.3 to 3.6. VNDegen loads the game's pack unchanged, from a `.pck` beside the `.exe` or from inside the `.exe`.
- Godot 4 draws through Metal on Mac, iPhone and iPad. Godot 3 draws through OpenGL on Mac and through ANGLE on iPhone and iPad. Godot needs a Mac with Apple silicon.
- Controllers reach the game as an Xbox controller, and touch and the mouse as Godot's mouse. A hardware keyboard types into the game's text fields, and the Mac keyboard and mouse wheel work.
- Saves go where Windows keeps them. `user://` is under the game's AppData stand-in, so Ludusavi backups from Windows, a Steam Deck, or Godot's Linux and Mac builds restore there. Games that save beside their `.exe` save in their own folder.
- Files outside the pack are found whatever case the game names them in.
- Games VNDegen can't run say why on their page: Godot C# games, encrypted packs, GDExtension and GDNative games, and games with Steam built in.

## Known limits

- A focused text field doesn't open the on-screen keyboard, and held keys don't repeat.
- `OS.alert()` writes to the log instead of showing a dialog.
- If Godot fails partway through starting a game, for example because its renderer doesn't start, it runs no more games until VNDegen is reopened.
- Godot 4 games written for the compatibility renderer run on the mobile renderer on Metal.
- Tested with the 4 Godot games in the library that VNDegen supports. All reach their title, save and load on the Mac and the iPad simulator, and one also on the iPhone simulator. `docs/godot.md` has the details.

More NScripter games run: ones with CD music, Lua scripts, packed voices and drawing plugins.

## Downloads

- `VNDegen-0.8.3-macOS.zip` for Mac (macOS 15 or later). It is ad-hoc signed: right-click VNDegen and choose Open the first time, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VNDegen.app`.
- `VNDegen-0.8.3.ipa` for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). Update it from the AltStore or SideStore source (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChronoStriker1/vndegen/main/altstore/source.json`), or sideload it with Sideloadly.

## New

- NScripter CD music plays from the game's `CD` folder (`track01.ogg` and on, or `.mp3` and `.wav`), the layout English releases ship. A disc isn't read.
- Games that script part of their logic in Lua (`system.lua` beside `nslua.dll`) run it on an embedded Lua 5.1. A game's Lua can't open files, run programs or load modules.
- Voices packed as NBZ files play, and archive entries packed with the engine's LZSS compression load.
- The `MSpDraw.dll` drawing plugin moves, turns, scales, tilts and fades pictures as its manual describes.
- An English release written for backquoted text lines shows them as English text wrapped between words, with its `|` marks as short pauses.
- `blt` and `ofscpy` draw straight onto the screen, as one game's ending credits use them.

## Known limits

- The `|` pause length is a guess, because the game that uses it ships no NScripter program to compare with.
- NSLua's direct drawing functions aren't emulated, and of `MSpDraw.dll` only the calls the tested games make are. `docs/nscripter.md` lists the rest.
- Tested with the 10 NScripter games in the library, 4 of them new. All reach their title, play, save and load on the Mac and the iPad simulator.

Fixes for NScripter games.

## Downloads

- `VNDegen-0.8.2-macOS.zip` for Mac (macOS 15 or later). It is ad-hoc signed: right-click VNDegen and choose Open the first time, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VNDegen.app`.
- `VNDegen-0.8.2.ipa` for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). Update it from the AltStore or SideStore source (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChronoStriker1/vndegen/main/altstore/source.json`), or sideload it with Sideloadly.

## Fixed

- NScripter transitions from the `breakup.dll`, `lngtwave.dll` and `trvswave.dll` effect plugins look as they do on Windows. Characters break apart and fly off, and screens ripple, instead of crossfading.
- MP3 music and voices play in NScripter games.
- NScripter's text input and yes/no boxes look and sit as they do on Windows, and input boxes take the size the game asks for.
- NScripter games keep their global variables, such as the save dates a game's own save screen shows, when VNDegen is closed or the system ends it in the background.
- NScripter saves made inside a game's subroutines load correctly, and stay byte-identical to the PC version's.
- NScripter sound is decoded on its own thread, so a slow decode can't cause a dropout.
- NScripter backgrounds no longer show black holes where a color matched the image's top-left pixel.

## Known limits

- Other NScripter effect plugins still crossfade. CD audio, MIDI music, Lua scripts and two rarely used archive compression types aren't supported, because no tested game uses them.
- Tested with the 6 NScripter games in the library on the Mac and the iPad simulator. All reach their title, play, save and load, and movies and dungeon walking hold 60 fps.

Gives sound to RPG Maker MV games that ship only Ogg audio.

## Downloads

- `VNDegen-0.8.1-macOS.zip` for Mac (macOS 15 or later). It is ad-hoc signed: right-click VNDegen and choose Open the first time, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VNDegen.app`.
- `VNDegen-0.8.1.ipa` for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). Update it from the AltStore or SideStore source (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChronoStriker1/vndegen/main/altstore/source.json`), or sideload it with Sideloadly.

## Fixed

- RPG Maker MV games that ship only Ogg audio, which is most of them, now have sound on Mac, iPhone and iPad. Before, VNDegen asked them for `.m4a` files they don't have, so they played silent. Encrypted audio and looping music work. MV games that ship `.m4a` files and RPG Maker MZ games play as before.

## Known limits

- Tested with an MV game with encrypted audio and one with plain Ogg files on the Mac and the iPad simulator. Music, background sounds, jingles and sound effects all play, and both hold about 60 fps on the map and in battle.

Adds NScripter games on Mac, iPhone and iPad, on VNDegen's own NScripter runtime, written for VNDegen and MIT licensed like the rest of the app.

## Downloads

- `VNDegen-0.8.0-macOS.zip` for Mac (macOS 15 or later). It is ad-hoc signed: right-click VNDegen and choose Open the first time, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VNDegen.app`.
- `VNDegen-0.8.0.ipa` for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). Update it from the AltStore or SideStore source (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChronoStriker1/vndegen/main/altstore/source.json`), or sideload it with Sideloadly.

## New

- NScripter games run inside VNDegen's window. VNDegen finds a game by its `nscript.dat`, or by a `0.txt` or `00.txt` script beside its archives, up to two folders down. The runtime reads `.nsa`, `.sar` and `.ns2` archives, including bitmaps NScripter's packer compressed, and plays Ogg and WAV sound and MPEG-1 movies.
- NScripter saves are the PC engine's own files, byte for byte, in the game's save folder. They move between VNDegen and a PC copy of the game, and Ludusavi backs them up.
- English translations whose patched engine wraps text between words get the same word wrap.
- NScripter games start with the Keyboard and mouse layout. Clicks and taps reach the game as NScripter's mouse buttons.

## Known limits

- MP3 and CD audio don't play. Effect DLLs, such as `breakup.dll`, fall back to a crossfade. NSLua games aren't supported, and the `MSpDraw.dll` layer plugin draws only what one test game needs.
- The built-in dialogs and the default save and load menus are VNDegen's own drawing, not Windows', so their layout differs from the PC version.
- A save slot's date is lost if VNDegen is force quit, because the game writes it with its global variables when it quits. Quitting normally keeps it.
- Tested with the 6 NScripter games in the library. All reach their title, play, save and load on the Mac and the iPad simulator, and one also on the iPhone simulator. Movies and dungeon walking hold 60 fps on the Mac and the iPad simulator.

Adds Flash games on Mac, iPhone and iPad, played by Ruffle, a Flash Player written in Rust. Games now find their files whatever case they name them in, Windows fonts get free substitutes with the same metrics, and VNDegen fits small and odd iPad windows.

## Downloads

- `VNDegen-0.7.0-macOS.zip` for Mac (macOS 15 or later). It is ad-hoc signed: right-click VNDegen and choose Open the first time, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VNDegen.app`.
- `VNDegen-0.7.0.ipa` for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). Update it from the AltStore or SideStore source (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChronoStriker1/vndegen/main/altstore/source.json`), or sideload it with Sideloadly.

## New

- Flash games run inside VNDegen's window. VNDegen finds a Windows projector (`Game.exe` with the movie inside), a `.swf` movie, or a collection's own HTML menu page, up to four folders down, and plays the projector's movie without unpacking it. A game's page offers its other movies under Start with, such as a loader or gallery unlock that ships beside the game.
- Flash games written in ActionScript 1, 2 and 3 work, drawn with WebGL on Metal.
- Flash saves are Flash's own `.sol` files, kept in the game's data folder by the movie that made them, and Ludusavi backups map them to and from Flash Player and Ruffle on a PC. The game writes them when it pauses, when VNDegen leaves the screen, and when it quits.
- In Flash games, the VNDegen menu, the touch gamepad, touch mouse, controllers and the keyboard all work. Flash games start with the Keyboard and mouse layout. A projector's Exit button returns to the library.
- Windows fonts. Games that ask for MS Gothic, MS Mincho, Arial, Tahoma and other Windows fonts by name get free fonts with the same metrics, as under Proton: Ume fonts for the Japanese ones, Liberation for Arial, Times New Roman and Courier New, and DejaVu for Tahoma. RPG Maker MV and MZ, TyranoScript, KiriKiri, RPG Maker XP, VX and VX Ace, and Flash games use them. Chinese and Korean substitutes are a download in Settings, Fonts. KiriKiri games without a default font of their own now use the MS PGothic substitute, as on Windows.
- iPad windows. VNDegen fits small and odd window sizes on iPad. The library, game pages, the in-game menu, the touch gamepad and every engine fit the window and stay clear of iPadOS's window controls. A game in a window follows the window's shape.

## Fixed

- Every engine finds a game's files and folders whatever case the game uses, as on Windows, on iPhone, iPad and case-sensitive Mac volumes. Before, a game that asked for `Img/Title.PNG` when the disk had `img/title.png` failed there. Saving to a name that exists in another case replaces that file instead of making a second copy.

## Known limits

- Ruffle's ActionScript 3 support is less complete than for ActionScript 1 and 2, so some AS3 games may stop or skip something. One test game needed a fix to Ruffle, which VNDegen includes.
- Flash microphone input doesn't exist.
- A Flash collection's HTML menu keeps the layout it had in a desktop browser.
- Tested with the 14 Flash games in the library. All reach their title and play on the Mac and the iPad simulator, and the 12 that save also save and load. One plays on the iPhone simulator.
- The iPad window layouts were checked on the iPad simulator at sizes down to 320 points wide and in real windows. Drag-resizing, tiling and Slide Over couldn't be driven in the simulator.
- The Chinese and Korean font downloads are 51 MB and 26 MB.

The whole app now works with a controller alone, with an on-screen keyboard the controller types on.

## Downloads

- `VNDegen-0.6.2-macOS.zip` for Mac (macOS 15 or later). It is ad-hoc signed: right-click VNDegen and choose Open the first time, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VNDegen.app`.
- `VNDegen-0.6.2.ipa` for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). Update it from the AltStore or SideStore source (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChronoStriker1/vndegen/main/altstore/source.json`), or sideload it with Sideloadly.

## New

- Every screen takes controller focus: the library, game pages, every Settings page, the button mapping editor, adding a game, the lock screen, and every dialog and sheet. A sheet that opens over another, such as a license over the artwork editor, gets focus too.
- Text fields open an on-screen keyboard when you press A on them. A types the focused key, X deletes, LB toggles shift, RB switches to symbols, Y finishes, and B closes it without changes. It covers the Ludusavi server fields and game search, metadata source keys and search, and the folder name and password when adding a game.
- Hidden games can be set up by controller: set, change or remove the passcode with the D-pad and A, and turn biometrics on or off.
- Adding a game by controller lists the archives in VNDegen's own folder. The Files and Photos pickers need touch or a mouse, and now say so on screen.
- The button mapping editor has Reset, which returns a game to its engine's default layout, and LB and RB jump between groups of buttons. Remapping A or B never changes how the editor or the VNDegen menu respond.
- License text scrolls by controller.

## Fixed

- On the Mac, Settings rows now show controller focus. Before, no row showed where focus was.
- The "Can't launch" alert closes with A or B. Before, a controller couldn't close it.

## Known limits

- Checked by controller alone on the Mac app and on iPad and iPhone simulators, with simulated controller input. Not yet checked with a real controller.
- Retrying Face ID with X wasn't tested, because the simulators have no biometrics. The Ludusavi game search wasn't tested against a real share.
- On iPhone and iPad, iOS may keep a controller's Home button for itself. The touch gamepad's house button and the corner menu button always open the VNDegen menu.

Adds mouse controls for controllers and fixes two RPG Maker MZ problems seen in No Socks RPG: looping cutscene clips that stuttered or drifted from their sound, and quick presses in timed attacks that didn't register.

## Downloads

- `VNDegen-0.6.1-macOS.zip` for Mac (macOS 15 or later). It is ad-hoc signed: right-click VNDegen and choose Open the first time, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VNDegen.app`.
- `VNDegen-0.6.1.ipa` for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). Update it from the AltStore or SideStore source (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChronoStriker1/vndegen/main/altstore/source.json`), or sideload it with Sideloadly.

## New

- Controllers and the touch gamepad can act as a mouse. Any button or stick can move the pointer, left or right click, turn the mouse wheel, or open the on-screen keyboard on iPhone and iPad. "Click" in the mapping editor is now "Left click".
- The mapping editor has four layouts to start from: "Keyboard and mouse", a copy of Steam's template of that name, "Mouse", "RPG Maker controls" and "Xbox gamepad". KiriKiri and TyranoScript games start with "Keyboard and mouse", since neither engine reads a gamepad. Sticks stay sticks in the other layouts.
- On iPhone and iPad, text typed on the on-screen keyboard reaches KiriKiri games, including their pop-up text windows, and web-based games. Pasted text with several lines arrives one line at a time.

## Fixed

- In RPG Maker MZ, short looping movies made from GIFs, such as the Ms. Mittens cutscenes in No Socks RPG, play at their real length. WebKit reads these files as shorter than they are and paused about 300 ms at every loop, so the clips stuttered and fell out of step with their sound. Each loop now matches the length stored in the file to within about 1 ms, including the first pass after a clip changes. Movie frames are also uploaded only when they change, which saves work on every frame. This fix is for RPG Maker MZ only.
- In RPG Maker MZ, quick presses from a controller, the touch gamepad or the keyboard all reach the game. Some games clear their input after each step of a timed attack, and VisuStella's Core Engine then ignored a controller for 24 frames, so the presses that followed were lost. A press and release within one frame was lost too. Both now register. In No Socks RPG's timed attacks, press slightly early: the game closes each hit's window on the exact frame the ring meets the outline.

## Known limits

- Mouse controls were checked on the iPad simulator and the Mac with simulated controller input, not yet with a real controller. Pointer speed, the stick dead zone and the pointer size may need tuning.
- The cutscene fix was checked on all 25 clips and all 9 scenes that show them, on the Mac app and the iPad simulator. The timed attack fix was checked on the iPad simulator and the Mac. Neither has been checked on a real iPad yet.

Adds KiriKiri games (KiriKiri 2 and KiriKiri Z) on Mac, iPhone and iPad.

## Downloads

- `VNDegen-0.6.0-macOS.zip` for Mac (macOS 15 or later). It is ad-hoc signed: right-click VNDegen and choose Open the first time, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/VNDegen.app`.
- `VNDegen-0.6.0.ipa` for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). Update it from the AltStore or SideStore source (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChronoStriker1/vndegen/main/altstore/source.json`), or sideload it with Sideloadly.

## New

- KiriKiri games run inside VNDegen's window. VNDegen finds them by `data.xp3`, an unpacked `data` folder, or an archive appended to the game's `.exe`, up to two folders down.
- The VNDegen menu, the touch gamepad, touch mouse, controllers and the keyboard all work. With a controller in KAG games, A is Return, B is a right click, Y and Menu are Escape, X holds Control to skip, and LB and RB page through the message history.
- Encrypted archives work with no per-game setup. VNDegen recognizes the common ciphers and says when a game uses one it doesn't know.
- Common Windows plugins are built in, including transitions, layerExDraw, layerExSave, PSB and emote images, and the plugins in Steam builds.
- Movies play: MPEG-1 and MPEG-2, WMV, and H.264 and HEVC with hardware decoding.
- Older KiriKiri 2 games get the script behavior they were written for, and a game's `.cf` settings file applies, so a game that moves its save folder keeps it there.
- Saves stay where the PC version keeps them: `savedata`, a save folder set in the `.cf` file, or the AppData and Documents folders. Ludusavi backups from Windows and the Steam Deck map onto them.
- Quitting a game, or VNDegen itself, lets the game save its system data, even with one of its Yes/No dialogs open. You can play any number of KiriKiri games one after another without restarting VNDegen.

## Known limits

- Sound effects and music stored as MP3 don't play. MP3 audio inside movies does.
- AlphaMovie (`.amv`) animations don't show.
- In a game's Yes/No dialog, the first D-pad press highlights Yes, so press it twice to reach No before pressing A. A Windows keyboard behaves the same way.
- If a Mac logs out or shuts down while a KiriKiri game is still starting with a question on screen, the settings from that moment aren't kept.
- One game's save thumbnails were black in a test run. It didn't happen again.
- Tested with nine KiriKiri games from the library. Six reach their title, play, save and load on the iPhone simulator. On the Mac, four of them were checked through save and load, and the other two through reaching their title and quitting with their saves written. Not yet tested on a real device.

## What works

- RPG Maker MV and MZ games, unmodified, with saves in the same `.rmmzsave` format as the PC version. Encrypted assets, WebM movies, and Effekseer effects play.
- The library hub with artwork and metadata from Steam, SteamGridDB, IGDB, and VNDB, and per-device layouts for iPhone, iPhone Duo, iPad, and Mac.
- Touch, mouse and keyboard, and game controllers. A controller drives the library, game pages, and their sheets. The Hidden games and Metadata sources settings pages still need touch or a mouse. On iPhone and iPad, an on-screen gamepad or virtual mouse appears when no controller is connected.
- Hidden games behind Face ID, Touch ID, or a passcode.
- In-game orientation lock: landscape by default on iPhone, and on iPad only when the app is full screen.
- Ludusavi backup and restore against an existing Ludusavi folder, including a network share connected in the Files app.
- Importing games from zip, RAR, and 7z archives with Add game.

## Adding games

- iPhone and iPad: Files, On My iPhone (or iPad), VNDegen, Games, one folder per game. Or use Add game with an archive.
- Mac: `~/Games/VNDegen`, one folder per game.

## Known limits

- Only RPG Maker MV and MZ games run so far. Other engines show as unsupported.
- Not yet tested on a physical iPhone, iPad, or controller.
- Password-protected RAR and 7z archives cannot be imported. Password-protected zips can.
